title: Subscription Invoice Fetcher
summary: Matches each row of a subscription/invoice breakdown sheet to the matching invoice email in an admin Gmail inbox, saves the attachment, and returns the sheet with a Status column and a link to each found invoice. It now finds the real header row even when a title/section label sits above it, and prefers whichever same-named column (e.g. two 'amount' columns) actually has real values when the sheet has ambiguous column names.
prompt: Every row is coming back as Missing Data on a real sheet. The cause: the sheet has a title/section label in row 1 (e.g. '20001  Software Subscriptions - Engineering') and the ACTUAL column headers are in row 2 (Sr No, Voucher Number, Invoice Date, Communication / Breakdown, Partner (Vendor), Debit, Breakup Amounts, Amount in dollars, Enterprise, Test Case (reference only)). The code currently does pd.read_excel(input_path) with no header row detection, so it always treats row 1 as the header — which is wrong here, so no column ever matches and every row is marked Missing Data. Fix: instead of assuming row 1 is the header, scan the first several rows (e.g. first 10) for the row that actually looks like a header — the one containing the most recognizable column-name keywords (enterprise/client/company/vendor, breakdown/description/communication, date, amount) — and use that row as the real header, skipping any title/label rows above it. Keep everything else the same (still uses the 'Enterprise' column for enterprise name, a breakdown/description column, an invoice date column, and an amount column).
assumptions: The real header row is always within the first 10 rows of the sheet, never further down
Each sheet has one header row, not headers split across two rows
When more than one column name matches a field's keywords (e.g. 'Breakup Amounts' and 'Amount in dollars'), the column with the most populated/parseable values in that data is the real one to use
A sheet with no row resembling a header anywhere in the first 10 rows is reported as unreadable rather than guessed at
gaps: No way to manually pick the header row if the automatic guess is wrong on a particular sheet
Sheets whose column names contain none of the recognized keywords are reported as unreadable, not processed by guesswork
Headers split across two separate rows are not supported
expects: The invoice breakdown sheet as a real .xlsx file, with a header row somewhere in its first 10 rows containing recognizable names for enterprise/client/company/vendor, a breakdown/description/communication column, an invoice date, and an amount
A Gmail App Password for the admin inbox (16 characters, spaces from Google's display are stripped automatically)

history.prompt: I have attached a template subscription invoice. Across every enterprise there is a breakdown against every break down i want the invoice gotten from the admin email around that date. The feature shall take admin account access and the invoice sheet and get invoices from the gmail against every break down.

Replace the current Google OAuth sign-in flow (which needs a Cloud Console app, GMAIL_CLIENT_ID/GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, and a redirect URI set up in advance) with a plain input field in the tool's own web page instead: an email address field and a Gmail App Password field (the 16-character password anyone can generate themselves from Google Account -> Security -> 2-Step Verification -> App Passwords, no developer setup needed). Use these two values to connect to the admin Gmail inbox over IMAP instead of the Gmail API/OAuth, and search for the invoice emails the same way as before. The app password field must be a masked password input, must never be written to disk or logged, and should only be held in memory for the current run (the user re-enters it each time they run the tool, same as they re-upload the sheet).

Sign-in is rejecting valid app passwords. The likely bug: Google displays the 16-character App Password with spaces every 4 characters for readability (e.g. 'abcd efgh ijkl mnop'), but the real password has no spaces. The current code only strips leading/trailing whitespace from the app_password field, not spaces in the middle, so a copy-pasted password with its original spacing gets sent to Gmail as-is and rejected. Fix: strip ALL whitespace from the app password (not just leading/trailing) before using it to sign in. Also update the on-page help text to mention that spaces in a pasted app password are fine and will be removed automatically.
